hypothesis: W-R50's order-invariant full-batch learner produced a partial gain driven by xorshift, not robust source transfer. Hold the W-R50 architecture/step budget/rubric fixed across three prospective independent synthetic development cohorts to determine how reproducibly batch learning outperforms two online orderings, without selecting a favorable trained model.
freeze: Freeze three development blocks 3216..3231, 3248..3263, 3280..3295 and untouched sealed heldout 3312..3359 (48). Same original W-R50 signed 1728 affine_prior training examples per block, 16 weights no intercept, zero init, 32 epochs, LR0.1, online original/reverse and full-batch commutative fixed-pre-epoch gradient. Score all nine pre-frozen trained arms on the same fresh heldout three generators/two swapped sites, 4-bit identity and XOR55. No cohort/model selection, refit or post-outcome thresholds.
measures: For each development block and arm archive exact weight SHA256, training corpus SHA, updates, balanced original-first/second accuracy, by-generator and 48-seed groups. Compute full-batch minus mean-online gain for each block and worst batch accuracy across blocks. Training cohorts are an explicit reproducibility axis; heldout seeds are shared/correlated, not independent validation cohorts.
criteria: BATCH_CROSS_TRAIN_ROBUST iff ALL THREE batches achieve >=0.55 balanced accuracy, >=0.02 improvement against their own two-online mean, and >=2 generator families >0.52 in every block. PARTIAL_REPLICATION iff >=2 batches have accuracy>=0.55 AND gains>=0.02 regardless of generator gate. OTHERWISE_NEGATIVE otherwise. Do not select best single cohort or silently alter W-R50 original outcome.
controls: Exactly frozen original W-R50 training and heldout scoring functions reused with patched only DEVELOPMENT and HELDOUT seed tuples before training, restored after calls; no outputs from heldout used in training
Each cohort train all three arms with exactly 1728 signed examples and 32 epochs; online/batch compute & update semantics differ and are acknowledged
Identity/XOR55 exact feature invariance, two-order balanced truth, ties half credit, no source family metadata in model
Archive first-use original output, one full Go test/build, no accepted references, independent FSA authority, merge or production activation
claim_limit: Reproducibility across synthetic training cohorts for a paired-choice readout; no single-stream cognition or physical-world source transfer.
